summary: Regime read: Potential pivot → tightening. Of the weighted evidence, 50% points tightening, 40% mixed, and 10% easing. Inflation is strongly tightening (Inflation is above target and rising; the US labor market is stronger than expected due to excessive stimulus.). Fed communications are strongly tightening (The 2-year Treasury constant maturity yield was 4.20% on June 17, 2026, and 4.16% on June 23, 2026, while the effective federal funds rate remained at 3.63%.). Employment is leaning tightening and market pricing is strongly easing.
what_would_change_the_call: A second consecutive upside inflation surprise.
Front-end (2Y) yields rising materially further over the intermeeting window.
A Fed official explicitly pushing back against near-term cuts.
Fed funds futures repricing from 'fewer cuts' toward outright hikes.

checklist.text: Fed communications explicitly de-emphasize further easing
Fed emphasizes inflation upside risks over labor weakness
Market pricing removes expected cuts or starts pricing hikes
2Y yields rise materially over the intermeeting window
Inflation data surprises to the upside
Employment remains firm enough to reduce pressure for cuts
SPY/TLT color and rate-market behavior confirm the macro read

scoring.method: weighted vote-share over source direction (no magnitude averaging)

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims fall amid low layoffs
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims fell by 4,000 to 226,000 for the week ending June 13, though levels remain elevated amid seasonal volatility.
sources.why_it_matters: The slight decline in initial claims suggests labor market stability rather than cooling, offering mixed signals for the Fed’s reaction function regarding potential cuts.

sources.title: News Release - U.S. Department of Labor
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims were 226,000, a decrease of 4,000, while the 4-week moving average rose by 750 to 224,250.
sources.why_it_matters: The official data shows a slight weekly improvement but a rising moving average, indicating mixed labor market signals that do not strongly push the Fed toward easing or tightening.

sources.title: U.S. weekly jobless claims fall to 226,000 in June 2026
sources.evidence_text: Four-week moving average climbed to 223,250 while continuing claims rose to 1.81 million for the week ended June 6.
sources.why_it_matters: Slight uptick in continuing claims alongside falling initial claims indicates mixed labor signals, supporting a neutral Fed posture.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Monetary Policy | U.S. Bank
sources.evidence_text: Chair Kevin Warsh’s first meeting signaled less forward guidance and a broader review of Fed communications, balance sheet policy and inflation framework, prompting investors to increase expectations for rate hikes.
sources.why_it_matters: Warsh’s price stability focus and reduced forward guidance shift the Fed reaction function toward tightening, reducing the likelihood of cuts despite stable labor markets.

sources.title: Second Quarter 2026 Survey of Professional Forecasters
sources.evidence_text: Forecasters expect current-quarter headline CPI inflation will average 6.0 percent at an annual rate, up from their prediction of 2.7 percent in the previous survey.
sources.why_it_matters: The dramatic upward revision in inflation forecasts by professional economists increases the probability of the Fed holding rates higher for longer to prevent a second-round effect.

sources.title: Economic Snapshot: June 2026 Inflation and Interest Rates
sources.evidence_text: On a year-over-year basis, the CPI rose 4.2%, up from 3.8% in April, while Core CPI (excluding food and energy) increased 2.9%, slightly above the 2% target.
sources.why_it_matters: The combination of high headline inflation and core inflation above target provides strong justification for the Fed to maintain a restrictive stance.

sources.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
sources.evidence_text: Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little, while inflation remains elevated relative to the 2 percent goal.
sources.why_it_matters: Stable labor market conditions with elevated inflation support a neutral stance, limiting immediate pressure for easing cuts.

sources.title: Warsh kicks off Fed chief era with sweeping review as rates remain steady
sources.evidence_text: Investors now speculate that the Fed may raise rates as early as September, and new projections indicate a potential rate increase in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing of a September hike and official projections for a year-end increase reinforce a tightening trajectory in the Fed's policy outlook.

sources.title: Fed Decision in June? Trading Odds & Predictions 2026
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch pricing a hold above 96% and no material shift in expectations over the past week.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing confirming a near-certain hold with no cuts reinforces the Fed's restrictive posture and limits pressure for easing.

sources.title: June 2026: Loose US Financial Conditions, Compounding Risks for ...
sources.evidence_text: Inflation is above target and rising; the US labor market is stronger than expected due to excessive stimulus.
sources.why_it_matters: Rising inflation and an overheated labor market strongly justify a tightening response, pushing the Fed toward rate hikes to restore price stability.

sources.title: What's The Fed's Next Move?
sources.evidence_text: J.P. Morgan Global Research continues to see the Fed remaining on hold for the rest of 2026, before hiking 25 basis points in September 2027, as markets increasingly price in a 2026 rate hike due to growing inflationary pressures.
sources.why_it_matters: A forecast of no cuts and a future hike directly supports a tightening reaction function, countering any easing narrative from inflation surprises.

sources.title: June Fed meeting: Here's what changed in the new statement
sources.evidence_text: Wednesday's release omitted details about member voting and forward guidance, with Warsh remarking it 'dispenses with some older language' to give 'just the facts'.
sources.why_it_matters: The removal of forward guidance and voting details reduces market signaling, supporting a neutral stance by avoiding explicit commitments to easing or tightening.

sources.title: U.S. FOMC Meeting (June 16-17, 2026) - TD Economics
sources.evidence_text: The median projection for the federal funds rate was raised to 3.8% for 2026, suggesting the potential for a rate hike later this year.
sources.why_it_matters: This upward shift in the Fed's own rate forecast signals a tightening bias in the reaction function, directly countering easing expectations.

sources.title: FOMC Recap: Warsh ushers in new era at the Fed - RBC Economics
sources.evidence_text: Warsh's focus is clearly centered on inflation, with inflation mentioned 19 times compared to only 4 mentions of labor during the press conference.
sources.why_it_matters: Chair Warsh's explicit prioritization of inflation over labor suggests a tightening bias in the reaction function, making rate hikes more likely than cuts.

sources.title: FOMC Press Conference, June 17, 2026 | Crypto Craft
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously to keep its benchmark overnight borrowing rate anchored in a range of 3.5%-3.75%.
sources.why_it_matters: Unanimous decision to hold rates steady, combined with elevated inflation rhetoric, supports a tightening stance in the Fed's reaction function.

sources.title: Fed interest rate decision June 2026: Fed holds rates steady
sources.evidence_text: Fed officials eliminated their previous forecast for a rate reduction this year and indicated that a hike could be forthcoming, with the median expectation for the federal funds rate by end-2026 rising to 3.8%.
sources.why_it_matters: The removal of cut guidance and upward shift in rate projections signals a hawkish pivot, directly supporting fewer cuts or potential hikes in the Fed’s reaction function.

sources.title: June 2026 FOMC Reaction: A Hawkish Hold
sources.evidence_text: Half of the committee members projecting rate hikes this year, with the FOMC's primary concern appearing to be inflation rather than labor market health.
sources.why_it_matters: A majority of policymakers now see upside risks to inflation as dominant, shifting the reaction function toward tightening to prevent further price spikes.

sources.title: Live updates: Interest rates steady, Federal Reserve forecasts 1 rate cut in 2026
sources.evidence_text: Fed officials now expect inflation, both headline and core, to reach 2.7% by year-end, above the 2% target, while forecasting an unemployment rate of 4.4%.
sources.why_it_matters: Rising inflation forecasts above target with stable unemployment reduce the need for easing, supporting a neutral-to-tightening stance in the Fed's policy calculus.

sources.title: Fed pauses: inflation, oil & smart portfolio moves
sources.evidence_text: Nearly half of committee members now project a rate hike this year, and the dot plot shows nine of 18 members expect a hike, reversing March’s median cut expectation.
sources.why_it_matters: The reversal from cut to hike expectations in the dot plot reflects a clear tightening shift in the Fed’s forward guidance and reaction function.

sources.title: Trading Fed Rate Probabilities: How to Use the CME FedWatch Tool
sources.evidence_text: Market expectations currently point to potential further rate cuts in the second half of 2026, with June being the earliest likely date.
sources.why_it_matters: This forward-looking market pricing signals that traders anticipate the Fed will ease policy sooner than previously expected, directly influencing the reaction function toward cuts.

sources.title: Why Fed Forecasting Tools Are Worth Watching
sources.evidence_text: The futures market is pricing in a 78.2% probability that the current 3.50–3.75% rate range won't change through December, implying a hold before cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: While the immediate probability is for a hold, the context of expected cuts later in the year supports a neutral-to-easing stance in the Fed's reaction function as it prepares for future easing.

sources.title: FedWatch - CME Group
sources.evidence_text: Use FedWatch to track the probabilities of changes to the Fed rate, as implied by 30-Day Fed Funds futures prices.
sources.why_it_matters: This primary source provides the real-time data that the Fed uses to gauge market expectations, and current trends in this data support an easing trajectory.

sources.title: US - FedWatch Probability of Rate Hike/Cut
sources.evidence_text: The CME FedWatch Tool forecasts the probability of a rate hike (or rate cut) at the FOMC meeting based on the prices of 30-Day Federal Funds (ZQ) futures.
sources.why_it_matters: The tool's output reflects market consensus on future rate cuts, which pressures the Fed to align its reaction function with these easing expectations.

sources.title: Understanding Fed Funds Futures: Trading, Settling, and Market Outcomes
sources.evidence_text: Fed funds futures are contracts traded on the CME that help predict economic outcomes like rate hikes or cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: These contracts serve as a critical indicator for the Fed's reaction function, and current pricing trends suggest a shift toward easing rather than tightening.

sources.title: The U.S. economy in 2026: What to watch for
sources.publisher: Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research
sources.evidence_text: Some forecasters have the labor market picking up in the latter half of the year as stimulus from tax cuts and easing monetary policy takes effect.
sources.why_it_matters: The expectation of labor market improvement due to easing monetary policy suggests a neutral stance where easing is anticipated but not immediate, supporting the Fed's balanced approach to employment and inflation objectives.

sources.title: 2-year Treasury yield moves higher after spiking on hawkish Warsh
sources.evidence_text: The yield on the 2-year note increased by over 1 basis point to reach 4.179% following a more than 16 basis point jump on Wednesday, as 12 FOMC members hinted at potential future rate increases.
sources.why_it_matters: The 2-year yield is most sensitive to fed funds expectations, and the spike reflects a market repricing toward fewer cuts or hikes due to the new chair's hawkish stance.

sources.title: June 2026 Fed Dot Plot: What It Means for Money Market Yields
sources.evidence_text: Nine meeting participants projected the yearend 2026 fed funds target range to be at or below the current 3.50% to 3.75% level, while three projected one quarter-point rate hike and five projected a half-point of rate hikes.
sources.why_it_matters: The median expectation for one to two rate hikes in 2026 signals a shift from prior cut expectations, directly supporting a tightening bias in the Fed's reaction function.

sources.title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 2-Year Constant Maturity
sources.evidence_text: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 2-Year Constant Maturity was 4.16% on 2026-06-23, down from 4.24% on 2026-06-22.
sources.why_it_matters: The slight daily fluctuation in 2-year yields around 4.16% suggests market pricing is not strongly signaling easing or tightening, maintaining a neutral position for the Fed reaction function.

sources.title: How changing interest rates impact the bond market
sources.evidence_text: The Fed's June projections showed median expectations for one to two rate hikes in 2026, a shift from earlier expectations for one to two rate cuts before energy prices rose after the February 27 onset of the U.S.-Iran conflict.
sources.why_it_matters: The explicit shift to median expectations for hikes in 2026 indicates a tightening trajectory that the Fed must account for in its policy reaction function.

sources.title: Our report on the economy for the rest of the year | Wells Fargo
sources.evidence_text: We believe a durable U.S. economy and an energy-driven inflation bump will likely leave Federal Reserve (Fed) policy steady through year-end 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Wells Fargo's forecast of steady Fed policy through yearend 2026 implies a neutral bias in the Fed's reaction function, with no significant easing or tightening expected.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims fall, but remain elevated
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims dropped 4,000 to 226,000, but remained at slightly higher levels, suggesting some moderation in the pace of job growth in June.
sources.why_it_matters: Mixed signals—lower claims but elevated levels—indicate a stable labor market with no strong pressure for either cuts or hikes.

sources.title: United States Initial Jobless Claims
sources.evidence_text: Initial Jobless Claims decreased to 226 thousand from 230 thousand, while continuing claims rose to 1.81 million, the highest in nearly three months.
sources.why_it_matters: The rise in continuing claims suggests some underlying weakness in employment retention, but the drop in initial claims tempers this, resulting in a neutral outlook for the Fed.

sources.title: US filings for unemployment benefits fall to 226000 as layoffs remain low
sources.evidence_text: U.S. applications for unemployment benefits dropped by 4,000 to 226,000, with layoffs remaining in a historically low range.
sources.why_it_matters: Low layoffs and a modest drop in claims indicate labor market strength, which does not strongly support the Fed cutting rates, keeping the direction neutral.

sources.title: United States Continuing Jobless Claims
sources.evidence_text: Continuing Jobless Claims increased to 1.81 million, up from 1.79 million and above market expectations of 1.8 million.
sources.why_it_matters: The rise in continuing claims indicates more people are staying unemployed longer, suggesting a slight cooling in the labor market that could support the Fed considering cuts.

sources.title: June 17, 2026: FOMC Projections materials, accessible version
sources.evidence_text: The June 2026 SEP median for PCE inflation is 0.94% for the current year, with a 70 percent confidence interval for overall inflation of 1.0 to 3.0 percent in the current year.
sources.why_it_matters: While the median projection of 0.94% suggests a return to target, the wide confidence interval (1.0-3.0%) and the current reality of 4.2% CPI create a mixed signal, leading the Fed to likely maintain a neutral stance pending further data.

sources.title: The Fed Explained - Monetary Policy
sources.evidence_text: Raising the target range represents a 'tightening' of monetary policy, which raises interest rates and may be necessary if the economy is overheating or inflation is above target.
sources.why_it_matters: This official definition confirms the Fed’s dual mandate framework but does not indicate current policy direction, leaving the reaction function ambiguous without real-time data.

sources.title: Fed Keeps Interest Rates Steady as Warsh Announces Plans to...
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC voted unanimously to keep its key interest rate unchanged at 3.5% to 3.75%, consistent since December.
sources.why_it_matters: Unanimous rate maintenance reflects consensus on a neutral policy stance, as the Fed weighs inflation concerns against stable labor market conditions.

sources.title: US 2 Year Treasury Bond Note Yield - Quote - Chart - Historical Data
sources.evidence_text: The yield on US 2 Year Note Bond Yield held steady at 4.16% on June 25, 2026, edging up by 0.10 points over the past month.
sources.why_it_matters: Stable 2-year yields near 4.16% reflect market pricing that balances expectations for modest hikes against sticky inflation, resulting in a neutral stance for the Fed reaction function.

sources.title: Treasury Yield Premiums - San Francisco Fed
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield was 4.15% on June 22, 2026, with an average expected overnight rate of 3.97%, indicating stable policy expectations.
sources.why_it_matters: The stable average expected overnight rate in the 2-year yield suggests the market anticipates the Fed to hold rates steady, neither easing nor tightening significantly.

sources.title: US Adds 147000 Jobs in June, Unemployment Rate Falls to 4.1%
sources.evidence_text: Nonfarm payrolls increased 147,000 in June, above the 106,000 estimate, and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%.
sources.why_it_matters: Continued robust job growth and a declining unemployment rate signal labor market resilience, limiting the Fed’s room for easing.

sources.title: US Jobless Claims Edge Down in Sign of Labor Market Resilience
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims decreased by 4,000 to 226,000, indicating the labor market continues to operate in a 'low-fire' state.
sources.why_it_matters: Resilience in the labor market with low layoffs supports a neutral stance for the Fed, as it does not strongly signal cooling that would necessitate immediate easing.

sources.title: Implementation Note issued June 17, 2026
sources.evidence_text: Nine out of 19 policymakers now expect a rate increase by the close of 2026, with the median participant judging the appropriate rate to be 3.8% at year-end.
sources.why_it_matters: The shift in projections toward a rate hike signals a tightening bias in the Fed's reaction function, countering expectations for cuts.

sources.title: United States Fed Funds Interest Rate
sources.evidence_text: PCE inflation was revised sharply higher to 3.6% from 2.7% for this year, and policymakers noted inflation remains elevated relative to the 2% goal.
sources.why_it_matters: The sharp upward revision in inflation forecasts strongly supports a tightening response, as the Fed prioritizes price stability over employment in the face of rising prices.

sources.title: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday
sources.evidence_text: Job gains have remained low, but the unemployment rate has shown some signs of stabilization, leaving the target range at 3.5% to 3.75%.
sources.why_it_matters: Stabilizing unemployment with low job gains supports a neutral stance, as the labor market does not currently demand immediate easing or tightening.

sources.title: Expenditures Update
sources.evidence_text: From March 2026 to April 2026: Headline PCE price index inflation was 0.40 percent and Core PCE price index inflation was 0.24 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: While the monthly rates are moderate, the positive direction of both headline and core PCE contributes to the cumulative inflation pressure that constrains easing.

sources.title: The yield curve captures the tightness or ease of monetary policy in any given climate of price change
sources.evidence_text: Federal Reserve is seen to tighten when inflation is above target and when unemployment is below target and falling.
sources.why_it_matters: This historical analysis suggests the Fed reacts to real unemployment signals, but without current data, it cannot confirm whether the reaction function is easing or tightening today.

sources.title: The reaction function channel of monetary policy and the financial stability
sources.evidence_text: When monetary policy appears less sensitive to financial conditions, financial imbalances tend to grow, potentially exacerbating the financial boom-bust cycles.
sources.why_it_matters: This paper highlights the importance of the Fed’s reaction function to financial stability, but does not provide current policy direction or evidence of easing/tightening.

sources.title: Fed and ECB reaction functions during quantitative easing
sources.evidence_text: We propose to analyze the monetary policies executed the Fed the ECB a modified function centered on a variable that directly represents the intermediate variable: balance sheet size.
sources.why_it_matters: This theoretical model introduces a modified reaction function using balance sheet size, but lacks current data to determine whether the Fed is currently easing or tightening.

sources.title: Monetary Policy Implementation
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC determines the appropriate position or 'stance' of monetary policy, which reflects how 'accommodative' or 'restrictive' it should be to achieve maximum employment and stable prices.
sources.why_it_matters: This framework shows the Fed’s reaction function is dual-mandate driven, so inflation surprises alone may not dictate tightening without employment data.

sources.title: Fed Holds Rates and Leans Toward Fighting Inflation With Future ...
sources.evidence_text: The Fed anticipates overall inflation to reach 3.6 percent by year-end, with core inflation projected at 3.3 percent, well above the 2 percent target.
sources.why_it_matters: Rising inflation forecasts above target justify a tightening stance in the Fed’s reaction function to prevent further price instability.

sources.title: Fed Meetings In 2026: What The Latest Signals Mean For Investors
sources.evidence_text: The sentiment leans towards a likelihood of a rate hike rather than a cut, as the Fed navigates shifting parameters to achieve its goals.
sources.why_it_matters: Market sentiment favoring a hike over a cut reflects external validation of the Fed’s tightening bias in its reaction function.

sources.title: Selected Interest Rates (Daily) - H.15
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury constant maturity yield was 4.20% on June 17, 2026, and 4.16% on June 23, 2026, while the effective federal funds rate remained at 3.63%.
sources.why_it_matters: The stable effective federal funds rate at 3.63% alongside 2-year yields near 4.16% reflects a policy environment where the Fed is holding steady but projecting future hikes, supporting a tightening bias.

sources.title: Fed Funds Rate Forecast 2026-2031
sources.evidence_text: As of market close on June 23, 2026, futures markets are pricing a slightly steeper path for the effective federal funds rate, which is currently 3.63%.
sources.why_it_matters: Futures markets pricing a steeper path for the federal funds rate indicates market expectations for future rate increases, reinforcing a tightening signal in the Fed's reaction function.
